sessions.phase_label: Initial demand drafting, approval, and dispatch
Certified-delivery tracking, remailing, and escalation drafting
Escalation timing, delivery outcomes, and engagement closeout

requirements.title: Formal Demand Letter
requirements.definition: Draft and finalize a formal demand and notice-of-default letter on the freelancer's letterhead that cites the relevant agreements, states the debt and enforcement position, and addresses the intended borrowers.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the content, addressees, review, and finalization of the initial demand document; physical delivery and borrower-facing email transmission are independently executable Requirements.

requirements.title: Certified-Mail Delivery of Demand Letters
requirements.definition: Send certified USPS copies of the demand letter to the required addresses, retain delivery evidence, and use client-approved replacement or alternate addresses when an attempted delivery fails.
requirements.boundary_note: The number of copies, destination addresses, proof of delivery, and approved remailings are attributes of one certified-delivery mechanism; drafting the letter and emailing it are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Initial Borrower Email Notice
requirements.definition: Send both borrowers an accompanying email with the demand letter, notify them of the certified mailing, and copy the client.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the initial electronic notice accompanying the original demand; later proactive escalation correspondence and replies to future borrower responses have different triggers and trajectories.

requirements.title: Escalation Follow-Up Notice Content and Approval
requirements.definition: Prepare, obtain client approval for, and send a proactive follow-up or escalation notice after the borrowers fail to respond, including the agreed delivery-history and updated-balance details.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a proactive second notice triggered by nonresponse and later described as beyond the original scope; it is not one of the contingent replies to an incoming borrower message.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Yael,

I hope this finds you well. Here is a brief summary.

In August 2023, Edwin Mason and John O’Brien executed a Secured Promissory Note for $1.23M, personally obligating themselves as borrowers. They also executed a Pledge & Security Agreement, pledging their equity interests in Meade Transportation, Inc. (MTI) and Virginia Freight Holdings, LLC (VFH). The Note carried a 30% interest rate with a 90-day maturity. When they failed to repay, it went into default in November 2023, triggering a 35% default interest rate.

As of October 1, 2025, the balance due is approximately $2.5M, with default interest accruing at over $1,100 per day. Despite repeated demands, they have not paid or provided an acceptable repayment plan, instead attempting to introduce “updated loan agreements” that would weaken my secured position and strip away their personal liability.

What I need is straightforward:

Prepare and send a formal demand letter on your letterhead to Edwin Mason and John O’Brien, citing their obligations under the Note and Security Agreement.

Send the letter via U.S. Certified Mail to establish formal delivery.

Send a follow-up email to both Edwin and John attaching the demand letter, notifying them of the certified mailing, and copying me.

To make this simple, I’ve attached:

A summary of events and balance calculation

A draft demand letter you can adapt

Copy of the Secured Promissory Note

Copy of the Pledge & Security Agreement

I’d like to have this completed within the next week and prefer a reasonable flat fee since the drafting work is largely done. My priority is issuing the demand formally on your letterhead to establish the record.

Please let me know your availability to speak and work out the flat fee.

value_updates.purpose: formally demand payment and establish a record of the borrowers' default and obligations

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi Faraz,

I’m enclosing the draft Final Demand and Notice of Default for your review before signature. It reflects all terms of the Note and Pledge & Security Agreement and outlines the enforcement steps, including foreclosure, arbitration, potential damages, and credit-impact language.

Please review and share any comments or revisions before I sign and issue the final version.

For reference, the official notice details from the Note are:
•	Stratagem Global Corporation / Edward Mason / John O’Brien
1717 K Street NW, Washington DC 20006
sgcadmin@protonmail.com

Best,
Yael

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports preparing a draft Final Demand and Notice of Default that reflects the Note and Pledge & Security Agreement and outlines proposed enforcement steps for client review.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Following our recent conversation, I reviewed the signed agreements. Both the Note and Security Agreement were signed by Stratagem Global Corporation, with Mason and O’Brien signing only as officers, not personally.

That said, I’d keep the demand letter as-is addressing them personally keeps leverage strong and doesn’t tip them off. If they deny liability later, we can still pursue fraud or alter-ego arguments based on their conduct.

And yes, I did find your email in my spam folder thanks for pointing that out!

Best,
Yael

ambiguity.description: The signed agreements appear to show Mason and O’Brien signing only as corporate officers, conflicting with the client's stated personal-liability premise and requiring a decision on whether the demand should continue addressing them personally.

source_message.text: That works.

source_message.text: Please share how the final and updated demand letter will look like in addition to how the email going out to the borrowers will look like

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Looks great, let’s get it sent .

Hi Yael —

I’m willing to proceed at \$625 if you can include the following:

Mail two certified USPS letters \(I will provide the two addresses\) and send one accompanying email confirmation to the two parties involved  when those letters are mailed.

Handle up to three email exchanges with the other party when they respond. I will draft the replies and you can send them on my behalf.

Complete everything by Monday.

Let me know if that works.

Thanks,
Raaz

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hello!

As you can see, one of the packages was received, while the other was returned to me. I received it this morning, which accounts for the delay in my response.

Upon further inquiry yesterday, I contacted the delivery service and requested that they verify all suite numbers in the building; however, they advised that no individual or entity by that name was located. I will therefore be sending a new copy, dated today, to the official corporate address.

I have also not received any response to my previous email. Once the new mailing has been sent and received at the company’s official address, it will be deemed officially delivered for all intents and purposes, and we can then consider your options at that point.
